sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: sponsor versus insurance, permit versus GDL passengers, the age ladder, day versus night windows and transfer deadlines
Confusable pairs across the Wisconsin license ladder, where many rules differ by only an age, an hour or a seat; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A01
The same birth certificate or passport can prove both your name and date of birth and your citizenship or legal status, but residence needs two separate Wisconsin address documents. [A01]
Why it matters: group documents; confusable one document versus two.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A03
A sponsor signs form MV3001 for an applicant under 18, and the behind-the-wheel school also supplies a signed MV3001, so the same form number appears twice in the teen path [A03] [A01].
Why it matters: group sponsorship; prereq driver education; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A02
Proof of insurance replaces a sponsor for certain minors, such as one with no living parent, whereas a listed relative may sponsor a teen who is not living with a parent or legal guardian. [A02]
Why it matters: group sponsorship; confusable insurance versus relative sponsor.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A02
A sibling or spouse may sponsor only if they are 18 or older, but a grandparent, aunt, uncle or foster parent has no stated age condition. [A02]
Why it matters: group sponsorship; confusable age condition.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A03
Adults 18 and older can get a permit by passing the knowledge test, signs test and vision screening, while teens also need to be at least 15 and enrolled in driver education. [A03]
Why it matters: group permit; confusable adult versus teen permit path.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A03
On a permit, a qualified instructor or a parent, guardian or spouse must be at least 19, but any other companion must be at least 21. [A03]
Why it matters: group permit; confusable nineteen versus twenty-one.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A03
The extra back-seat licensed passenger allowed on a permit must be at least 25, whereas the front-seat companion can be as young as 19. [A03]
Why it matters: group permit; confusable twenty-five versus nineteen.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A03
Every permit companion needs at least two years of licensed experience on a valid regular license; a probationary or occupational license does not qualify. [A03]
Why it matters: group permit; misconception any licensed adult.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A04
Permit practice needs 40 daytime hours and 10 darkness hours, so the 50-hour total cannot be met with daytime driving alone. [A04]
Why it matters: group supervised driving; misconception daytime only.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A04
Before a probationary license, a teen needs six months on the permit, a sixteenth birthday and proof of driver education, so turning sixteen alone is not enough. [A04]
Why it matters: group probationary; prereq permit; misconception age alone.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R11 | anchor: A05
In the 5 a.m. to 12 a.m. window a GDL driver may go anywhere alone, but in the 12 a.m. to 5 a.m. window driving alone is allowed only between home, school and work [A05] [A04].
Why it matters: group GDL; confusable day versus night window.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-R12 | anchor: A04
Immediate family members are unlimited as passengers during the daytime GDL window, while other riders are limited to one qualifying licensed adult plus one other person. [A04]
Why it matters: group GDL; confusable family versus non-family passengers.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R13 | anchor: A05
The GDL limits normally last nine months, but a moving violation, a breach of the limits or a suspension or revocation adds six more months. [A05]
Why it matters: group GDL; confusable nine months versus six-month extension.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-R14 | anchor: A05
Renewal of the regular license is every eight years and may be done up to one year early, while the probationary-to-regular renewal window opens 90 days before expiration. [A05]
Why it matters: group renewal; confusable one year versus ninety days.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-R15 | anchor: A06
A new resident has 60 days to apply for a Wisconsin regular license but only 30 days for a commercial license. [A06]
Why it matters: group transfers; confusable sixty versus thirty days.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-R16 | anchor: A06
A REAL ID card is marked with a star, and from May 7, 2025 a passport is an accepted alternative for domestic flights and federal buildings. [A06]
Why it matters: group REAL ID; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0012]
